inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: The “15-point ceasefire plan” sent to Iran through Pakistan looks more like a managed trap than a serious attempt to stop the war: set the terms, then blame Iran if the fighting continues. Iran’s five counter-conditions put responsibility and costs on the table, including ending aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Israel’s skepticism and insistence on pre-emptive strikes make the public peace talk look even more like cover. The powerful players want negotiations they can control while keeping escalation ready, with blame assigned in advance.
